text:
marta: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel ladder change I see an uptick in p99 for small seq (<64) on canary. p99 ~48ms -> ~78ms on node-group C.

alex: ugh. is that correlated with the new micro-batch window jitter tweak? which commit?

marta: correlated. commit 6f3b2a2 adjust coalesce jitter sampling to gaussian. also saw KV cache hit-rate dip ~6% in profiler around same time.

sam: can you paste the flamegraph snippet? rough numbers ok.

marta: profiler (sampled ~2k reqs):
```
kernel_select.rs             26%
coalesce_scheduler          18%
kv_cache::fetch             12%
rpc::serialize              9%
others                      35%
```

marta: coalesce_scheduler CPU +11%, kv_cache::fetch tail widened.

jing: maybe gaussian jitter increased microbatch churn -> more KV evictions; heavier tails mean more late singleton batches.

alex: can you repro with fixed seed + compare params? run loadgen --coalesce-delay-ms 3 --jitter-mode fixed and --jitter-mode gaussian

marta: running now against canary, will paste numbers.

(deploy-bot): canary: deployment 2024-11-02T09:12:34Z started — tag=service/coalesce-gauss-6f3b2a2

marta: results:
- gaussian: p50 22ms p95 65ms p99 79ms kv-hit 83%
- fixed:    p50 20ms p95 48ms p99 50ms kv-hit 89%

jing: eviction count spikes align with jitter tails; eviction rate +2.5x under gaussian.

sam: short-term: lower jitter sigma or cap max delay; also smooth token-budget in kernel selector so it doesn't downgrade kernels on transient drops.

alex: agree. actions:
- marta: hotfix reduce gaussian sigma 6ms -> 2ms and add --coalesce-max-delay-ms 8
- sam: prototype token-budget EMA (1s) in kernel selector to avoid flip-flop
- jing: add prometheus panel for eviction-rate and kv-hit sliding window

marta: PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/1298 includes flag and sigma change.

(deploy-bot): canary: deployment 2024-11-02T09:47:10Z succeeded — tag=service/coalesce-gauss-hotfix-1298

marta: post-hotfix quick run: p95 49ms p99 52ms kv-hit 88% (improved)

sam: good. still want the token-budget smoothing spike.

alex: create short runbook doc with recommended coalesce params for small-seq workloads and add to /docs/runbooks/coalesce-tuning.md

marta: will add to runbook :memo:
